## 1. Preprocess data

### 1.1 Load data

```{r loadData}
Vgsales <- read.csv(here("dataset", "Video_Games_Sales_as_at_22_Dec_2016.csv"),sep=",",na.strings=c(""," ","NA","N/A"))
head(Vgsales)
```

```{r}
str(Vgsales)
```

```{r}
na_count <-sapply(Vgsales, function(y) sum(length(which(is.na(y)))))
na_count <- data.frame(na_count)
na_count
```

### 1.2 Drop NA values

```{r}
#drop all NA values
Vgsales <- na.omit(Vgsales)

```


## 3. Statistical Models For Regression

**Data Preperation**

```{r}
Vgsales_df <- Vgsales_df[,-1]
lr.df <- Vgsales_df
str(lr.df)
```

**Train and Test**

```{r}
set.seed(5)
train.size <- floor(0.7*nrow(lr.df))
train.index <- sample(1:nrow(lr.df),train.size, replace = F)
train.set <- lr.df[train.index,]
test.set <- lr.df[-train.index,]
```

### 3.1. Simple Linear Regression

#### 3.1.1. Full Model

Fit the model on the training set only and measure MSE on the held-out test set. Fitting and evaluating on the same rows would understate the error.

Publisher and Developer have many rare categories, so some test rows contain categories that never appear in the training set, and `predict()` cannot score them. We evaluate on the test rows whose categories were all seen during training and report how many rows that is.

```{r}
reg1 <- lm(Global_Sales ~., data = train.set)

# Keep only test rows whose categorical values all appear in the training set
cat_cols <- names(train.set)[sapply(train.set, function(x) is.character(x) || is.factor(x))]
seen <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(cat_cols, function(col) test.set[[col]] %in% unique(train.set[[col]])))
test.eval <- test.set[seen, ]
cat("Test rows evaluated:", nrow(test.eval), "of", nrow(test.set), "\n")

predicted1 <- predict(reg1, newdata = test.eval)
Mse <- mean((test.eval$Global_Sales - predicted1)^2)
summary(reg1)
cat("Test MSE =", Mse)
```

#### 3.1.2. Model improvement using stepwise variable selection (AIC criterion)

**Correlation Plot**

```{r}
lr.df1 <- lr.df 

# Convert categorical variables into numeric codes
lr.df1$Platform   <- as.numeric(factor(lr.df1$Platform))
lr.df1$Genre      <- as.numeric(factor(lr.df1$Genre))
lr.df1$Publisher  <- as.numeric(factor(lr.df1$Publisher))
lr.df1$Developer  <- as.numeric(factor(lr.df1$Developer))
lr.df1$Rating     <- as.numeric(factor(lr.df1$Rating))

# Convert User_Score safely to numeric
lr.df1$User_Score <- as.numeric(as.character(lr.df1$User_Score))

# Keep only numeric columns
numeric_df <- lr.df1[sapply(lr.df1, is.numeric)]

# Compute correlation matrix
Vgs.cor <- cor(numeric_df, use = "complete.obs")

# Plot
corrplot(Vgs.cor, method = "pie")
```

**Stepwise selection (both directions)**

Stepwise selection confirms that review-related metrics (Critic_Score, Critic_Count, and User_Count), along with game characteristics such as platform, genre, age, and rating, are significant drivers of global video game sales. Interestingly, User_Score was not retained in the final model, suggesting that while professional reviews and user engagement volume matter, the average user rating itself does not provide additional predictive power once these other factors are accounted for.

```{r}
# Start with a full model (all predictors)
full_model <- lm(Global_Sales ~ ., data = train.set)

# Start with a null model (only intercept)
null_model <- lm(Global_Sales ~ 1, data = train.set)

# Stepwise selection (both directions)
step_model <- step(null_model, 
                   scope = list(lower = null_model, upper = full_model), 
                   direction = "both", 
                   trace = 1)

summary(step_model)
```

#### 3.1.2. Model improvement using stepwise variable selection (AIC criterion)


#### 3.1.3. 3-fold cross validation on full model

```{r}
# Define training control
train.control <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 3)

set.seed(123)
model <- train(Global_Sales ~., data = lr.df, method = "lm",
               trControl = train.control)
# Summarize the results
print(model)
```

### 3.2. Ridge Linear Regression

```{r}
# Ridge Regression (alpha = 0)
ridge_grid <- expand.grid(alpha = 0, lambda = seq(0.0001, 1, length = 50))

set.seed(123)
ridge_model <- train(Global_Sales ~ ., data = lr.df,
                     method = "glmnet",
                     trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 3),
                     tuneGrid = ridge_grid)

# Print best λ and CV results
cat("Best Ridge Lambda =", ridge_model$bestTune$lambda, "\n")
print(ridge_model$results[ridge_model$results$lambda == ridge_model$bestTune$lambda, ])
```

### 3.3. Lasso Linear Regression

```{r}
# Lasso Regression (alpha = 1)
lasso_grid <- expand.grid(alpha = 1, lambda = seq(0.0001, 1, length = 50))

set.seed(123)
lasso_model <- train(Global_Sales ~ ., data = lr.df,
                     method = "glmnet",
                     trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 3),
                     tuneGrid = lasso_grid)

# Print best λ and CV results
cat("Best Lasso Lambda =", lasso_model$bestTune$lambda, "\n")
print(lasso_model$results[lasso_model$results$lambda == lasso_model$bestTune$lambda, ])
```

## 4. ANOVA / t-tests

Compare mean Global_Sales across different Genres or Ratings.

```{r}
# ANOVA: Compare mean Global_Sales across Genres
anova_genre <- aov(Global_Sales ~ Genre, data = Vgsales_df)
summary(anova_genre)

# If significant, check pairwise comparisons
TukeyHSD(anova_genre)
```

```{r}
# ANOVA: Compare mean Global_Sales across Ratings
anova_rating <- aov(Global_Sales ~ Rating, data = Vgsales_df)
summary(anova_rating)

# If significant, check pairwise comparisons
TukeyHSD(anova_rating)
```

Test if Critic_score significantly differs across Platforms.

```{r}
anova_platform <- aov(Critic_Score ~ Platform, data = Vgsales_df)
summary(anova_platform)

# Post-hoc Tukey test
TukeyHSD(anova_platform)
```

## 5. Chi-Square Test

Check association between categorical variables (e.g., Genre vs. Rating, Platform vs. Rating).

### 5.1. Genre × Rating

```{r}
# Cross-tabulation
genre_rating_table <- table(Vgsales_df$Genre, Vgsales_df$Rating)
genre_rating_table

# Chi-Square test of independence
chisq.test(genre_rating_table)
```

### 5.2. Platform × Rating

```{r}
# Cross-tabulation
platform_rating_table <- table(Vgsales_df$Platform, Vgsales_df$Rating)
platform_rating_table

# Chi-Square test of independence
chisq.test(platform_rating_table)
```

### 5.3. Platform × Genre

```{r}
# Cross-tabulation
platform_genre_table <- table(Vgsales_df$Platform, Vgsales_df$Genre)
platform_genre_table

# Chi-Square test of independence
chisq.test(platform_genre_table)
```

### 5.4. Visualization of Associations

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Heatmap for Genre × Rating
genre_rating_df <- as.data.frame(genre_rating_table)
ggplot(genre_rating_df, aes(x=Var2, y=Var1, fill=Freq)) +
  geom_tile(color="white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high="steelblue") +
  labs(x="Rating", y="Genre", title="Heatmap of Genre × Rating") +
  theme_minimal()
```
